facts.text: Healthcare and social services is Nanaimo's largest employment sector with 7,460 jobs, and retail is second with 7,380 jobs for local residents.
In 2022 the City had 3,610 businesses with employees, and about 87% of them, or 3,140 businesses, employ between 1 and 19 people.
facts.publisher: City of Nanaimo, 2023 State of the Nanaimo Economy

facts.text: Construction (18.9%), retail trade (12.6%) and professional, scientific and technical services (12.6%) lead Nanaimo's business licences, with the top five sectors making up 65% of licences.
School District 68 and Vancouver Island University are two of Nanaimo's largest employers, and Nanaimo Regional General Hospital serves the tertiary needs of 450,000 people.

overview: Nanaimo grew to 99,863 residents in the 2021 Census, a 10.3 per cent rise from 90,504 in 2016. The median age of 45.2 is higher than most Canadian cities, and households reported a median total income of $75,500 in 2020, so buyers tend to be older, careful and loyal once won.

The city covers only 90.45 square kilometres, so the 43,164 occupied dwellings sit close to one another and to the mid-island customers who drive in from surrounding areas. With 3,610 employer businesses competing in 2022, most of them very small, a clear local presence separates a firm from the rest.
